graph_edits.rationale: Preserve the dominant curved gesture but make the bend slightly more continuous and less blocky in section by tightening the longitudinal sweep.
Increase the curvature modestly so the mass reads as a stronger ribbon-like gallery spine rather than a generic bent bar.
Deepen the access-side carve to strengthen public threshold legibility at the verified frontage.
Widen the notch so the ground response becomes a clearer entry seam/court and less of a token cut.
Extend the carve vertically to better register as a public void connected to the civic sequence.

rationale: The candidate reads as one coherent dominant curved/bar mass across all four views, so it clears the single-gesture and multi-view coherence bar. The silhouette is not a literal stair stack; it is a continuous bent form with one strong carved recession, which is massing-credible for an early cultural diagram. The main weakness is program semantics at the ground edge: the blue frontage/access edge is acknowledged, but the visible response is mostly a sealed curved body with only a modest seam/notch, so the public threshold and gallery-sequence logic are underdeveloped for a museum. Still, the form can plausibly support cultural/public use, especially as a compact gallery spine with a carved entry/court condition. The mass is cleanly contained and not visibly self-colliding, and the reference set supports curved, terraced, and void-based cultural precedents.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced, site-responsive cultural massing with a legible carved public realm and layered circulation.
Simple elevated civic mass with strong void/overhang contrast and clear public ground reading.
